sd_galaxy_the.blurb: A compact cluster of short granite formations in the Needles of Custer State Park, forming the southern end of Moonlight Ridge. Climbs here are brief and set close together, mostly bolted at short intervals, with a few lines that want nuts and cams. About two dozen routes split between sport, top-rope and a small trad group. Difficulty starts near 5.5 and bunches up in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with a couple of harder ones above that, so it works well for newer leaders and anyone stacking up easy mileage before moving on to the taller Needles spires.

sd_palmer_gulch.blurb: A quiet, adventurous trad zone at the southern edge of the Needles of Rushmore country in the Black Hills, in the drainage below Harney Peak. Getting in takes a trail walk of more than a mile, which keeps traffic low; expect some lichen and loose bits on routes that rarely see a rope. Nearly all of the two dozen or so lines are gear-protected, with a couple of bolted ones and a single boulder problem. The grade spread leans hard: most routes fall between 5.11 and 5.12, a few moderates sit at 5.9 and 5.10, and a couple go beyond that. Winter brings an ice flow on the peak.

sd_boxelder_forks.blurb: A crack-climbing venue in the hills near Nemo, northwest of Rapid City, reached by a short trail from the creekside campground road. Around twenty trad lines run up to about 100 feet, many of them clean splitters ranging from fingers to offwidth, so bring a wide rack. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.10, with the bulk around 5.8 and 5.9. Tops are not bolted: finish on gear, trees or by walking off. The routes see little traffic, and although most have been cleaned of big loose blocks, treat the rock with some caution. A west-facing wall sits farther up the trail.

sd_rough_blocks_buttress.blurb: A steep limestone sport crag in Spearfish Canyon in the northern Black Hills, a short uphill hike from the Roughlock Falls trail lot. About twenty routes carry roughly ten to twelve bolts each and mix technical, gym-like sequences with old-school adventure. Expect pockets, crimps, pinches and sustained, pumpy climbing. Grades start at 5.8, but this is mainly a place for strong climbers: most lines fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with a few at 5.13. Not a warm-up spot, so arrive fit and ready to fall; mornings are the pleasant time to be here.

tn_jimmywood.blurb: One of the most visited sectors at Foster Falls, a sandstone cliff near Jasper on the Cumberland Plateau, west of Chattanooga. A broad ledge divides it into two zones. Most of the roughly two dozen climbs are bolted, with a few trad lines mixed in. It is a go-to spot for moderates: the bulk of routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, only a single route reaches 5.12, and a couple sit around 5.7. Good for climbers working through their 5.9s and 5.10s, but it can get crowded, especially when the weather is nice.

tn_broom_wall_rasputin_ledge.blurb: A steep, demanding section of North Clear Creek in the Obed and Clear Creek country of the Cumberland Plateau. Big roofs and long routes define it, and easy warm-ups are scarce. Most of the twenty-odd climbs are bolted, with a smaller trad group, and the grades sit firmly at the top end: nearly all between 5.11 and 5.13, with one easier line around 5.8. The walk in follows a ridge trail, and the base is rocky and shale-like in places. Best suited to strong, experienced sport climbers who want sustained overhanging terrain rather than a relaxed day.

tn_west_cliff.blurb: A short line of high-quality sandstone at Dogwood West, outside Dayton on the Cumberland Plateau. Most of the twenty-five or so routes are bolted, with a handful of trad lines, and the technical climbing leans on underclings, sidepulls and slopers. Grades run from easy 5.6 up to 5.13a, though the heart of the cliff is 5.10 to 5.12, so it rewards intermediate and strong sport climbers more than complete beginners. The cliff is modest in height, the walk from the lot is brief, and the atmosphere is low-key, with plenty of boulders nearby for a mixed day.
